title: Thailand Tourism Demand Forecast
thesis: Snowflake turns daily room-night demand and booking pace flags for a fictional Thai hotel group into flag and early sell-out KPIs, 7-day early sell-out risk scores, a network room-night forecast, pickup forecast error anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on one governed platform.

talking_points: Flag-free day rate, booking pace flags raised, early sell-outs and room revenue in THB for 40 fictional hotels in Bangkok, Phuket, Chiang Mai, Pattaya and Krabi.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to property-day rows.
The flag-type chart shows which pace flags end in early sell-outs and which are always resolved, such as flight disruptions.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of room-night demand KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which properties should the revenue team watch first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores the probability that each property sells out early in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
The forecast projects network-wide room nights for 14 days, and anomaly detection flags pickup forecast error outliers per property.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Are our revenue controls keeping up?

talking_points: Pickup review adherence, allotment confirmation coverage and pending confirmations frame the control gaps.
Pickup review adherence against early sell-outs by property shows where missed reviews and sell-outs coincide; it is a synthetic association, not proof of cause.
The action memo is drafted by an LLM from the KPI, property, pace-flag-type and risk rows only, and needs human review.
tabs.call_out: Grounded AI drafts, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What is happening on the booking channels right now?

talking_points: Simulated channel booking events land in RAW.LIVE_BOOKINGS: through Amazon Data Firehose, S3 and Snowpipe in the AWS build, or APP.SIMULATE_BOOKINGS in the Snowflake-only build.
PACE_FLAG events are short-lead, high-value bookings; the alert logs them with an SOP hint and the current risk band, then emails the on-call revenue analyst.
The lag card shows the time from send (or generation) to table.
tabs.call_out: Live bookings and alerting on the same platform as the KPIs

transition.line: Can the team just ask questions of this data?

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic pace flag SOPs for procedures.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOP IDs it cites.
Try: Which 3 properties have the most early sell-outs, and what SOP applies to the top one?
tabs.call_out: Answers grounded in governed data and documents

talking_points: Both architectures are shown, the current build first: Snowflake only, or AWS Firehose, Bedrock and QuickSight on Snowflake.
Every flow in the diagrams is created by the scripts in the repository, from a seeded synthetic generator.
Alerts, tasks and the app service stay suspended between demos.
tabs.call_out: One platform for data, ML, search, agents and the app

transition.line: Back to the cockpit for questions.
